content:
Plan for Phase 71b (safe config edits) at docs/phases/safe-config-edits.md, on branch phase-71b-safe-config-edits. The roadmap heading was renamed "Phase 71b: Safe config edits" for a clean slug (not started, nothing depends on it by name).

Decisions to review:
1. A closed safe set: gatekeeper.enabled, gatekeeper.on_submit, panel.enabled, briefer.enabled (booleans) and watcher.resend_minutes (integer >= 0). Everything else is refused with "edit by hand".
2. A narrow line locator. It finds one top-level `block:` line and one key line at the child indent, and replaces only the scalar (indent, spacing and trailing comment kept byte for byte). An absent key is inserted after the header; an absent block is appended. Flow or scalar blocks, duplicates, block scalars, tabs, and anchors/aliases are refused, never guessed. CRLF and a missing trailing newline are preserved.
3. Validation before any write. (a) The new text parses. (b) The parsed old and new configs are equal apart from the target key, which backs up the locator itself. (c) The engine's own resolver on the new config yields the requested value; otherwise the edit is refused with the resolver's reason (for example, enabling the panel without a headless reviewer). Turning something off always succeeds (the way out of a broken config). A request already in effect is a no-op.
4. A guarded write, as for the orders file: read-only refusal, no symlinks, O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW temp file with the mode kept, plus a compare-and-swap re-read before replace so a hand edit is never silently overwritten. Never creates tagteam.yaml.
5. CLI: `tagteam config keys` / `config set KEY VALUE [--preview]`. The preview prints a unified diff plus what the engine will do, and the two reads are allowed read-only. Cockpit: POST /api/config/set with a preview that returns the diff (shown in the confirm with the CLI line), strict JSON types (the Phase 71 r1 lesson), and On/Off switches plus a re-send field on the rows the payload marks editable.
6. tagteam.yaml stays IN the impl scope check (a phase may legitimately change config).

Open question: refusing an enable the engine would not honour, rather than writing it with a warning.

Reviewed docs/phases/safe-config-edits.md at 175aeb6 against the existing runtime resolvers, cockpit action path, safe_read and writer_lock. The closed safe set, narrow formatting-preserving editor, strict JSON types, read-only previews and keeping tagteam.yaml in scope are appropriate. I support refusing an enable that the resolver cannot honour; no arbiter decision is needed for that design choice.

Please resolve these plan-level correctness gaps before implementation:

1. [P2] Define no-op and editing from SAVED values, separately from effective resolver values (Validation step 3; Rules controls). A request "already in effect" must not skip persisting the requested value. Concrete current-resolver example: gatekeeper.enabled is true and scope is invalid, so resolved enabled is false. A request to disable must write enabled: false, not return "already false"; otherwise repairing scope later silently re-enables the gate. Likewise an invalid watcher block can resolve to 15 while its saved resend_minutes is 3. Define a no-op using the saved, correctly typed target value, and continue checking the resulting resolver separately. Expose saved/edit values as well as effective values for the new controls, including absent/invalid saved fields, so a user can persist OFF when an invalid block already resolves OFF. Add explicit acceptance cases for this and for repairing the other problem afterwards. Qualify "off always succeeds" as subject to the declared file/layout safety refusals, which must still apply.

2. [P2] Bind the cockpit confirmation to the bytes that produced its preview (Cockpit + Writing). The proposed body has only key/value, and the apply-time re-read protects only computation within that request. If tagteam.yaml changes after the preview but before the user confirms, apply will recompute on the new file and write a change the displayed diff did not describe. Return a source revision/digest with the preview and require it on the confirmed write (carried through the CLI action path), with a stale-preview refusal and a fresh preview before retry. Pin the sequence preview -> external file edit -> confirm: the new file must remain unchanged and the page must not silently retry the write.

3. [P2] Serialize config writers; a re-read followed by os.replace is not atomic compare-and-swap (Writing lines 103-106). Two CLI/API writers can both read A, compute different edits, both pass their final equality check against A, and then replace in succession, losing the first successful edit. Specify a shared thread/process lock for the actual read/validate/check/replace critical section, used by all new config writes; previews remain lock-free reads. Keep the final guarded re-read for edits made by external tools, but describe its limit accurately: an uncooperative external editor can still race between that check and replacement. Add a deterministic interleaving test for two writes to different safe keys, requiring both edits to survive or one to be explicitly refused.

Small validation clarification to include while revising: removing only the leaf from both parsed trees leaves a newly appended block as {}, so the stated deep comparison rejects the promised absent-block insertion (old has no watcher, new has watcher: {}). Define expected-tree comparison or narrowly normalize just the newly introduced target parent; do not normalize unrelated empty mappings. Cover absent and empty target blocks.

This is a plan review; no full suite was run. Read-only probes confirmed the saved-enabled/effective-disabled example and the absent-block comparison mismatch. No arbiter interjections or advisory standing orders were present.

All r1 findings are addressed in docs/phases/safe-config-edits.md (latest commit on the branch).

1. Saved vs effective (new section). A no-op is decided on the SAVED typed value only: absent | invalid | set. An effective OFF never turns a disable into a no-op, so gatekeeper.enabled:true + invalid scope → `set … false` writes false, and repairing scope later leaves the gate OFF. The resolver check is separate. It is required for an enable and for resend_minutes; a disable needs none, and "off always succeeds" is now stated as "never refused by the engine check", with every file/layout refusal still applying. /api/rules editable rows carry edit.{key, kind, saved, saved_state}; the control shows the saved value, and the row says "saved: on · not in effect: <reason>" when they differ. Criterion 8 (a) gate/scope then repair, (b) watcher 3-vs-15: a no-op names the problem, 5 is refused, then fix by hand and 5 writes, (c) an invalid saved value is written as a real false.

2. Bound to the preview. The preview reports `base` (the sha256 of the bytes it diffed). `config set --expect SHA` refuses when the bytes under the lock hash differently (exit 1 / HTTP 409, "preview again; nothing written"). The page always sends the base it showed, and on refusal it reports and never retries. Criterion 10: preview → an external edit → confirm is refused, the file keeps the external edit byte for byte, and there is no second POST (API and real Chromium).

3. One lock. The whole read/locate/validate/re-read/replace section runs under dualwrite.writer_lock(root) (thread RLock + fcntl.flock, the lock every cycle/state write takes); previews and keys stay lock-free. The final re-read's limit is stated honestly: an uncooperative external tool can still race between it and os.replace, and only that tool taking the lock would close it. Criterion 11: a deterministic interleaving (A paused inside the section by a test hook, B verified blocked, both edits survive), run with threads and with processes.

Tree check: expected = deepcopy(old) with the target set, normalising ONLY the target's own parent (absent, or empty `watcher:` → None → {}); then new == expected. Criterion 9 covers absent and empty target blocks, with an unrelated empty block left untouched.

Approved the revised plan at 3b496be.

All round-1 findings are addressed: saved, correctly typed values determine no-ops and editor state independently of resolver output; disabling persists OFF even when validation already disables the feature. Confirmed cockpit writes carry the preview's source digest, checked under the writer lock, and stale previews are refused without an automatic retry. All new config writers share the thread/process writer_lock across read/validate/re-read/replace, while previews remain read-only and lock-free. The remaining race with uncooperative external editors is accurately documented. Expected-tree validation handles absent/empty target parents without normalizing unrelated blocks.

The explicit acceptance cases for saved versus effective settings, stale confirmations, absent blocks, and deterministic thread/process write interleavings are sufficient to guide implementation. The closed safe set and refusal of ineffective enables remain approved. No remaining blocking plan findings.

Plan review only; no tests were run. No arbiter interjections or advisory standing orders were present.
